The '''Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit (BGS) conjecture''' also known as '''the random matrix conjecture''') for simple [[Quantum mechanics|quantum mechanical]] systems ([[Ergodicity|ergodic]] with a [[classical limit]]) few [[degrees of freedom]] holds that spectra of time reversal-invariant systems whose classical analogues are [[Kolmogorov automorphism|K-systems]] show the same fluctuation properties as predicted by the GOE ([[Gaussian orthogonal ensemble]]s).<ref>{{Citation |last1=Bohigas |first1=O. |chapter=Characterization of Chaotic Quantum Spectra and Universality of Level Fluctuation Laws |title=Spectral Distributions in Nuclei and Statistical Spectroscopy |pages=420–423 |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1142/9789814287395_0024 |access-date=2025-03-06 |publisher=World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd. |isbn=978-981-4287-39-5 |last2=Giannoni |first2=M. J. |last3=Schmit |first3=C.|date=2010 |doi=10.1142/9789814287395_0024 |doi-broken-date=1 July 2025 |chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bohigas |first1=O. |last2=Giannoni |first2=M.J. |last3=Schmit |first3=C. |date=1984 |title=Spectral properties of the Laplacian and random matrix theories |url=https://doi.org/10.1051/jphyslet:0198400450210101500 |journal=Journal de Physique Lettres |volume=45 |issue=21 |pages=1015–1022 |doi=10.1051/jphyslet:0198400450210101500 |issn=0302-072X}}</ref>{{Explain|reason=Too technical, full of undefined terms|date=March 2025}}

Alternatively, the spectral fluctuation measures of a classically chaotic quantum system coincide with those of the canonical random-matrix ensemble in the same symmetry class ([[Gaussian unitary ensemble|unitary]], orthogonal, or [[Gaussian symplectic ensemble|symplectic]]).{{Explain|reason=Too technical, full of undefined terms|date=March 2025}}

That is, the [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian]] of a microscopic analogue of a classical chaotic system can be modeled by a [[random matrix]] from a Gaussian ensemble as the distance of a few spacings between [[eigenvalues]] of a chaotic Hamiltonian operator generically statistically correlates with the spacing laws for eigenvalues of large random matrices.{{Explain|reason=Too technical, full of undefined terms|date=March 2025}}

A simple example of the unfolded quantum energy levels in a classically chaotic system correlating like that would be [[Sinai billiard]]s:{{Explain|date=March 2025|reason=Too technical, full of undefined terms}}

*Energy levels: <math>-\frac{\hbar^2}{2\mathit{m}}\bigtriangledown^2\psi+\mathit{V}(\mathit{x})\psi={\mathit{E}_\mathit{i}}\psi</math>{{Definition needed|date=March 2025}}
*Spectral density: <math>\rho(\mathit{x})=\sum_\mathit{i}\delta(\mathit{x}-\mathit{E}_\mathit{i})</math>
*Average spectral density: <math>\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rangle</math>
*Correlation: <math>\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle-\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rangle\langle\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle</math>
*Unfolding: <math>\rho(\mathit{x})\rightarrow\frac{\rho(\mathit{x})}{\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rangle}</math>
*Unfolded correlation: <math>\frac{\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle}{\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rangle\langle\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle}-1</math>
*BGS conjecture: <math>\frac{\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle}{\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rangle\langle\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle}-1=\frac{\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle_\operatorname{RMT}}{\langle\rho(\mathit{x})\rangle_\operatorname{RMT}\langle\rho(\mathit{y})\rangle_\operatorname{RMT}}-1</math>

The conjecture remains unproven despite supporting numerical evidence.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}
